IBM's revenue rose 4.7% to $17.10 billion. The growth rate is low, so the mix matters more. Software reached $7.80 billion, Red Hat grew 11%, and OpenShift is now a $2.4 billion ARR business. title: Salesforce vs. International Business Machines: Which Technology Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
detail:
Salesforce vs. International Business Machines: Which Technology Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
Jake Lerch, The Motley Fool
Mon, October 26, 2026 at 11:50 AM EDT 6 min read
CRM
IBM
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Choosing between Salesforce (NYSE:CRM) and International Business Machines (NYSE:IBM) in 2026 requires balancing the high-growth potential of a cloud software leader against the steady reliability of a diversified technology veteran.

Salesforce dominates the software landscape by helping companies manage customer data through the cloud. IBM has transformed itself into a specialist in hybrid cloud and consulting. Both companies are now competing for enterprise dollars by embedding artificial intelligence into their core service offerings.

The case for Salesforce

Salesforce sells a comprehensive suite of cloud-based tools that allow companies to manage sales, customer service, and marketing on a single platform. The business focuses on driving adoption across its various software modules, particularly among large enterprise clients. In its latest annual report, the company noted that no single customer accounts for more than 10% of total revenue, which reduces the risk associated with relying on any one client.

In its latest annual report, filed for the fiscal year ended Jan. 31, 2026, revenue reached nearly $41.5 billion. This represents a growth rate of approximately 9.6% compared with the prior fiscal year. Net income for this period climbed to roughly $7.5 billion. This growth suggests the company is successfully upselling existing clients to more advanced tech stocks within its ecosystem.

As of its January 2026 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio was approximately 0.3x. This ratio measures total debt relative to shareholders' equity, and a lower number indicates a more conservative use of borrowed money. The current ratio, which compares short-term assets to short-term liabilities, stood at roughly 0.8x. Free cash flow for the period reached close to $14.4 billion. Note that stock-based compensation accounted for roughly 23.4% of operating cash flow, inflating reported cash generation, since SBC is a non-cash expense added back to cash flow in the cash flow statement.

The case for International Business Machines

International Business Machines focuses on providing hybrid cloud infrastructure, consulting services, and enterprise AI tools. The company serves a diverse global client base, ranging from small businesses to large governments, across more than 175 countries. About 60% of its total revenue is generated outside the United States, showcasing its deep reach into international markets and its reliance on a global network of partners.

In its latest annual report, filed for the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, revenue reached nearly $67.5 billion. This was an increase of roughly 7.6% compared with the prior fiscal year. Net income for the period was approximately $10.6 billion. The growth reflects a strategic shift toward recurring software revenue and high-margin consulting contracts that help other businesses modernize their legacy technology systems.

Investing.com — Kyndryl Holdings Inc (NYSE:KD) is mounting an aggressive comeback. Trading near $14.86 per share, the enterprise IT infrastructure provider is up nearly 32% over the past month, shaking off years of post-spinoff skepticism.

The move draws obvious comparisons to the MicroStrategy playbook: taking an overlooked legacy tech company and pulling off a radical strategic reinvention. Left for dead after spinning off from IBM in 2021, Kyndryl has systematically purged low-margin contracts while building a $2 billion cloud business alongside AWS, Microsoft, and Google.

Even after its sharp October rally, the stock trades at just 6.8 times forward earnings and 0.19 times sales.

That combination of improving profit margins and deep valuation discounts is why ProPicks AI models added Kyndryl to both the Tech Titans and Mid-Cap Movers strategies.

Alongside Kyndryl, the models are currently targeting several other overlooked tech leaders—including a high-speed data center networking specialist and a key chip-manufacturing equipment supplier—that display the same cash-flow inflection.

See the tech turnarounds models are targeting alongside Kyndryl: Explore the Tech Titans strategy on InvestingPro

How shedding legacy baggage unlocked enterprise margins

When Kyndryl separated from IBM, the market largely dismissed it as a low-margin legacy services business burdened with unprofitable contracts.

However, management has spent the last 36 months systematically overhauling its revenue mix through a disciplined turnaround strategy. The company has aggressively scaled back low-margin IBM hardware reselling—cutting that exposure from $4 billion annually at the time of the spinoff to under $2 billion—while channeling resources into high-margin consulting and hybrid cloud architectures.

Crucially, Kyndryl is converting its massive Fortune 100 customer base into high-value cloud partnerships. Hyperscaler-related revenue has expanded from zero at the spinoff to approximately $2 billion annually, supported by deep enterprise alliances with Microsoft Azure, Amazon Web Services, and Google Cloud. Advisory signings inside its Kyndryl Consult division jumped 50% year-over-year in the latest quarter, driven by commercial wins like a 10-year government cloud contract and enterprise automation deployments with Toyota and WPP.

At the same time, internal automation has driven structural cost savings. Kyndryl has deployed roughly 1,800 proprietary AI agents across its infrastructure platform, generating approximately $1 billion in cumulative operational savings. As legacy contracts roll off, management projects these efficiency gains will lift free cash flow to $1 billion by 2028.

IBM (IBM) has recently been on Zacks.com's list of the most searched stocks. Therefore, you might want to consider some of the key factors that could influence the stock's performance in the near future.

Over the past month, shares of this technology and consulting company have returned +12.4%, compared to the Zacks S&P 500 composite's -1.2% change. During this period, the Zacks Computer - Integrated Systems industry, which IBM falls in, has lost 18.5%. The key question now is: What could be the stock's future direction?

Although media reports or rumors about a significant change in a company's business prospects usually cause its stock to trend and lead to an immediate price change, there are always certain fundamental factors that ultimately drive the buy-and-hold decision.

Revisions to Earnings Estimates

Here at Zacks, we prioritize appraising the change in the projection of a company's future earnings over anything else. That's because we believe the present value of its future stream of earnings is what determines the fair value for its stock.

We essentially look at how sell-side analysts covering the stock are revising their earnings estimates to reflect the impact of the latest business trends. And if earnings estimates go up for a company, the fair value for its stock goes up. A higher fair value than the current market price drives investors' interest in buying the stock, leading to its price moving higher. This is why empirical research shows a strong correlation between trends in earnings estimate revisions and near-term stock price movements.

IBM is expected to post earnings of $4.63 per share for the current quarter, representing a year-over-year change of +2.4%. Over the last 30 days, the Zacks Consensus Estimate has changed +0.7%.

The consensus earnings estimate of $12.41 for the current fiscal year indicates a year-over-year change of +7.1%. This estimate has changed +0.7% over the last 30 days.

For the next fiscal year, the consensus earnings estimate of $13.24 indicates a change of +6.7% from what IBM is expected to report a year ago. Over the past month, the estimate has changed +0.1%.

With an impressive externally audited track record, our proprietary stock rating tool -- the Zacks Rank -- is a more conclusive indicator of a stock's near-term price performance, as it effectively harnesses the power of earnings estimate revisions. The size of the recent change in the consensus estimate, along with three other factors related to earnings estimates, has resulted in a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) for IBM.

A 50% fall in IonQ (IONQ) stock is a real risk, because it has happened before. Shares dropped at least that far within the year in four of the last five calendar years, posting a median worst yearly fall of 52.2%. They are down 43.6% over the past year, while the S&P 500 gained 15.1%. IonQ also just priced a $2.0 billion share sale, which its CEO said will speed up the commercialization of its full-stack quantum platform. Below are the events most likely to move IonQ stock over the next six months.

In its favour

IonQ's First Revenue Outlook With SkyWater Included

During its August 5, 2026 call, management said IonQ's next revenue outlook will cover the combined company with SkyWater, the chip foundry it bought on July 31, 2026. The current guide, which the company raised in August to $280 million to $290 million for fiscal 2026, covers IonQ alone.

The combined number will not simply add the two companies together. IonQ expected to spend about $120 million with SkyWater in fiscal 2026, which counts as revenue for SkyWater. Management noted that standard accounting requires intercompany transactions to be eliminated in consolidation, and that finance teams are actively working through these eliminations and purchase-price adjustments post-close before issuing a combined target.

Customers Getting IonQ's 256-Qubit Machines

Management said on the August 5 call that IonQ plans to start commissioning customer systems built on its 256-qubit technology in the first half of 2027, a window that ends after the six months covered here. The company received its first fully integrated processors back from SkyWater for testing in the second quarter of 2026.

System sales already matter. Management said deployments of its fifth-generation computers at customers such as KISTI in Korea and QuantumBasel in Switzerland, were the largest reason second-quarter revenue beat its own expectations. IonQ ended June with $485 million of remaining performance obligations, representing revenue under contract but not yet booked. The commissioning schedule, updated at each quarterly report, is the thing to watch.

International Business Machines (IBM) stock trades at 21.4 times earnings. That gives the company the second-highest valuation in a group of five companies that also includes Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon.com and Accenture. Over each company's latest four fiscal quarters, however, IBM ranks fourth of the five in revenue growth. So what does the extra price buy you at IBM?

What You Get For IBM's Premium Over Accenture

Compared with Accenture, the only peer in IBM's own industry, you pay extra at IBM for a wider margin rather than faster growth. Accenture trades at 17.9 times earnings. Over each company's latest four fiscal quarters, IBM grew revenue 6.8% and Accenture grew 6.5%, close to a tie. IBM's operating margin was 18.3%, against 15.8% for Accenture, so IBM keeps more of each sales dollar as profit.

On growth alone, IBM's premium is harder to explain against the rest of the group. Alphabet grew revenue 20.1% and trades at 15.9 times earnings, but its earnings over those quarters ran far above its operating profit, which makes that multiple look cheaper than its business. Microsoft is the only peer priced above IBM, at 29.1 times, and it also grew faster, at 17.8%.

How Fast Is IBM's Software Business Growing?

IBM's software business is the largest part of the company. It grew 10.6% to $30.0 billion in fiscal 2025, faster than its consulting arm. Consulting, the second-largest business at IBM, grew 1.8% to $21.1 billion over the same year.

In fiscal Q3 2026, management said software revenue growth picked up to 9% at constant currency. That was four points faster than the quarter before. Within software, Red Hat grew 11%, and transaction processing, the software that runs on IBM's mainframes, grew 10%. Management also said the z17 mainframe has generated more than $1 billion of extra revenue over six quarters compared with earlier models.

Beyond the margin, that appears to be the other thing you pay extra for: IBM's largest business is growing faster than the company as a whole.
